item.title: Florida turns recruiting momentum into commitment from 2027 OT Moreno Fisher
item.description: Florida has landed one of the fastest-rising offensive linemen in the 2027 class. Moreno Fisher , a 6-foot-7, 270-pound offensive tackle out of Cornelius (N.C.) Hough , has committed to Jon Sumrall and the Gators following his official visit to Gainesville. The former Virginia commit saw his recruitment take off this fall. Auburn , Florida and Florida State were among the major programs to extend offers after Fisher reopened his recruitment. But Florida made its move early, and the Gators never let up. Fisher first visited Gainesville in September for the Ole Miss game. That trip gave Florida momentum, and offensive line coach Phil Trautwein continued building on it. Now the Gators have landed another offensive lineman for their 2027 recruiting class. “The experience and the whole environment of that game was something crazy,” Fisher previously told Rivals. “It was a daytime game, and it was still packed out. No open seats in the crowd. It was a great experience, honestly.” That first visit helped Fisher see Florida differently. The atmosphere impressed him, but the coaching staff ultimately helped separate the Gators from the competition. Trautwein made Fisher a priority from the moment Florida offered. The Gators’ offensive line coach stayed in regular contact, explained his vision for Fisher’s development and established a strong relationship with the North Carolina standout. “I like Coach Trautwein a lot. He has coached some great offensive linemen. Since offering me, he has recruited me hard. He is a top coach.” Sumrall also made a strong impression. Fisher followed Florida’s progress throughout the season and liked how the Gators responded to adversity. “Coach Sumrall has done a great job,” Fisher said. “They have a great atmosphere at Florida. The crowd is great. It is a top SEC school and the coaches have them playing well.” Florida’s staff continued making Fisher feel wanted after his September visit. Sumrall, Trautwein and other staff members maintained weekly communication, and the Gators made an in-person stop to see Fisher ahead of his official visit. That consistent attention mattered. “Honestly, it’s because of how they make me feel, coming from a coaching staff standpoint and a player standpoint,” Fisher said. “They make me feel like a priority.” Fisher also took notice of the direction of the program. “Then the way they carry themselves so far this season, bouncing back from losses, responding. It’s all just right in front of me. I like what they are about.” By the time Fisher returned to Gainesville for his official visit, Florida had established itself as the program to beat. The Gators used that opportunity to finish the job. Fisher’s commitment gives Florida a massive offensive tackle prospect with considerable upside. At 6-foot-7 and 270 pounds, he brings the length and frame that college programs covet at the position.

item.title: Real Madrid complete their first signing of the 2027/28 season – report
item.description: Real Madrid complete their first signing of the 2027/28 season – report According to MARCA , Real Madrid have completed an agreement to sign Ghanaian midfielder Latif Issman from UD Logrones, with the youngster set to join Castilla next summer. The deal was finalised today, making the 20-year-old the club’s first acquisition for the 2027-28 campaign. Real Madrid tracking Issman since the summer Issman, who is represented by MS Sports, has been on Real Madrid’s radar since the summer. The Spanish capital club made an attempt to sign him towards the end of the summer window, but were unable to get the deal across the line. However, having missed out on his signing in the summer, Los Blancos stepped up their efforts in recent weeks and have now been successful in reaching an agreement with UD Logrones. The two clubs already have a working relationship, having negotiated the transfer of Manex Rezola to Valdebebas last winter. Issman’s current contract with UD Logrones runs until June 30, 2027, meaning his move to Real Madrid will coincide with the end of his existing deal. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Rising Football Pros (@risingfootballpros_gh) Previous reports suggested that the midfielder had a release clause worth €300,000 in his contract with Logrones. For now, it is unclear if Real Madrid have paid that sum or negotiated a lower fee, or will be signing Issman for free. Who is Latif Issman? Born on November 1, 2006, Issman began his development at SD Logrones before moving to UD Logrones at youth level. He made the step up to the senior squad in July 2025 and gradually established himself as an important part of the team. Unai Mendia gave him playing time in all four matches during the promotion play-offs. His involvement increased further following the club’s promotion to RFEF Primera Federacion , where he has featured in ten games, even registering one assist. The 20-year-old Ghanaian talent also has one appearance in the Copa del Rey this season. Latif Issman will be Real Madrid’s first signing for next summer. (Photo by Gonzalo Arroyo Moreno/Getty Images) As per the report, Real Madrid’s interest is understood to have been driven by Issman’s physical presence and ability to break opposition lines. The midfielder attracted offers from several clubs, but the Merengues moved decisively to secure his signature. He is viewed as a potential long-term option in the No. 8 role at Valdebebas. His ability to provide balance in a double pivot, while also making forward runs and contributing to attacks, makes him an appealing profile for Castilla. With his signing for Real Madrid now completed, the next step for Issman will be adapting to the demands of the club’s reserve team when he arrives next summer.

item.title: Arsenal hold Barca to women's Champions League draw
item.description: Barcelona's Norwegian forward Caroline Graham Hansen pulled the holders level with Arsenal before the hour mark (MANAURE QUINTERO) Arsenal earned an impressive 1-1 draw at women's Champions League holders Barcelona on Thursday in a league phase clash between two of the competition's heavyweights. Caroline Graham Hansen secured four-time champions Barca, who have reached the final six seasons running, a point after Frida Maanum fired visitors Arsenal into a surprise lead at Camp Nou. The Gunners beat Barcelona in the 2025 final in Lisbon in the teams' last meeting and, despite Renee Slegers's team's domestic struggles, dug deep to deliver on the big stage again. The draw leaves Barca, second, level on 10 points with leaders Lyon after four matches, while the Londoners are fourth, level on eight points with third-place Bayern Munich and Chelsea. Two-time winners Arsenal had a golden opportunity in the opening stages when Caitlin Foord broke into the box but Irene Paredes blocked brilliantly. The rebound fell to Alessia Russo, who headed against the post from point-blank range, but appeared to be offside. Barcelona took control after that, with Graham Hansen and Sydney Schertenleib forcing Arsenal's Misa Rodriguez into two saves at her near post. The visitors, who are languishing in sixth in the English top flight, rode out the barrage and nosed ahead through Maanum after 22 minutes. Barcelona goalkeeper Cata Coll saved well from Foord but Norwegian midfielder Maanum reacted quickest to latch on to the rebound and slot home. Graham Hansen ran Arsenal left-back Taylor Hinds ragged but Barca could not break through before the interval. Claudia Pina fired narrowly wide after a burst inside from the left and Paredes looped a header over the crossbar. Graham Hansen's header clipped the post just before the break as Pere Romeu's Barca went in frustrated, but the Norwegian winger pulled them level before the hour mark. Esmee Brugts found Graham Hansen in the box and she cut inside Steph Catley and whipped a strike into the top left corner. Russo might have put Arsenal back in front but hammered over when well placed after being teed up by substitute Olivia Smith. Arsenal resisted Barcelona pressure in the final stages to end the hosts' 100 percent start to the competition. rbs/ea

item.title: Providence to host women's basketball franchise in spring 2027
item.description: PROVIDENCE — Women's professional basketball is coming to Amica Mutual Pavilion beginning in May. That's when the UpShot League will debut downtown, with Providence officially awarded an expansion franchise at a Thursday morning press conference in the venue's front lobby. Managing partner Mark Walsh said the Providence franchise will play its home opener May 13, part of a 28-game schedule that will run through the spring and summer. The league debuted in 2026 with four teams and is in the process of adding new markets ahead of its 2027 return. More: Rhode Island’s new UFL team has a name. Meet the Breakers "This is your team," Walsh said. "We want this to be your team. We are not asking for any money from the community — we are asking you for support." Gov. Dan McKee, Providence Mayor Brett Smiley and House Speaker Joseph Shekarchi were among the state political delegation gathered Thursday. They joined several executives from the Rhode Island Convention Center — CEO Dan McConaghy, chairman Ernest Almonte and general manager Larry Lepore. The state's basketball community was represented by former Providence College basketball star Ernie DiGregorio, former Johnston High and Friars standout Chelsea Marandola and former Providence players Harold Starks and Quinton Burton. "Providence is a great basketball city and it just became greater because of today's announcement," Smiley said. Walsh attempted to position the Providence franchise as a professional replacement for the Connecticut Sun, which played its last WNBA game 48 days ago and will relocate to Houston. Providence was among the cities that made both a presentation and formal offer to that team's owners in an attempt to keep them in the region. Discussions soon pivoted to the UpShot delegation while attempting to fill more dates downtown outside the traditional fall and winter schedules played by the Providence College men and Providence Bruins. "This team will give women a great opportunity to continue improving their basketball skills and to grow within the sport," Almonte said. "It will give players, coaches and referees a stage to showcase their talents and potentially move up to the WNBA." McKee attended the press conference with his daughter, Kara, a former player in their hometown of Cumberland. She was part of the first all-girls league in their community and developed into a state champion prior to her entry into high school. McKee asked her to recruit five classmates while starting their first team. That number eventually grew to more than 100 girls participating. "Full circle to be standing here at the AMP," McKee said. "A win for women's sports, a win for our capital city and a win for Rhode Island. Welcome." What is the UpShot League? The UpShot League was founded by Florida-based Zawyer Sports & Entertainment in January 2025. Investors include women's basketball greats Cheryl Miller, Ann Meyers Drysdale and Tamika Catchings and former Florida standout Patric Young. Jacksonville

item.description: A new head coach will roam the sidelines. A franchise icon will make his long-awaited return. An All-Star will begin his redemption tour. And a new ownership group will watch its first season opener from Paul Allen’s former seats along the Moda Center baseline. The Blazers open the 2026-27 NBA season Wednesday night against the Phoenix Suns — a team they upset in April in the play-in tournament — and if you’re just now tuning in for the start of the regular season, well, there’s a lot you missed. item.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
item.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. RELATED : Can the Ducks bounce back from UCLA loss? Experts release new Oregon vs. Nebraska predictions It’s not uncommon for teams with grand expectations to unravel in tough times. So far, that hasn’t happened. “The team is very connected and maintains its composure whether we’re winning or losing,” punter Bailey Ettridge said. “We haven’t let the losses last week and against Oklahoma State bring us down. I think we’ve handled them well.” Wide receiver Dakorien Moore said the team is filled with players who came to Oregon to win and be great. He added that the team’s goals remain attainable, and team leaders have worked to encourage togetherness and mutual trust. “If you can’t trust your teammate, then everything ain’t going to form in the way that it’s supposed to,” he said. This also means trusting the process, the plan and the team’s goal to get better instead of blaming one another. item.description: Oregon Ducks quarterback Dante Moore will miss the rest of the season, coach Dan Lanning announced Monday night. “I’m not anticipating him being back this season,” Lanning said. “Really got clarity for us this past week, for him,” Lanning added. “And I think if it were up to Dante in any shape, way, he would want to be out there playing for the guys. But, unfortunately, it’s not really up to Dante. It’s not really up to me. We can control the setting and practice where he’s able to do things for us, but that’s not always the case in the game.” Lanning said he expects Moore, who has run scout-team offense in practice, to fully recover. “That hasn’t changed,” Lanning said. “Definitely feel that way, but for him to be out there on the field for us right now, that’s not gonna happen.” Lanning added that Moore would remain involved with the team. “He’s still going to be a big part of this team and helping us move forward and find opportunities for us to be better,” Lanning said. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. item.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. item.title: The Risk the Tigers Are Taking on Emilio Pagan
item.description: The Detroit Tigers have agreed to a one-year deal worth $11 million with relief pitcher Emilio Pagan, a deal the New York Post first reported . Pagan is 35 and turns 36 during the 2027 MLB season, and he is the favorite to take over the ninth inning in Detroit after the Tigers declined their 2027 club option on Kenley Jansen . Pagan declined a $10 million player option with the Cincinnati Reds for the 2027 season. The move got him at least $1 million more than the option he turned down. Addressing the bullpen was a good thing for Scott Harris. Whether Detroit picked the right arm to do it is the question. Cincinnati Reds pitcher Emilio Pagán (15) cheers after striking out Tommy White for the final out of the ninth inning of the MLB Interleague game between the Cincinnati Reds and the Athletics at Great American Ball Park in downtown Cincinnati on Wednesday, Aug. 5, 2026. The Reds won the second game of the series, 3-2. He was carted off the field after a single pitch on May 5 , and the Reds did not have him back on the active roster until June 30 . Pagan pitched in 45 games for Cincinnati last season. item.title: Nelly Korda shoots bogey-free 63 in return at The Annika
item.description: Nelly Korda opened The Annika with a bogey-free 7-under 63 on Thursday at Pelican Golf Club. It was her first start since the Solheim Cup in mid-September. The world No. 1 made five birdies on the front nine to turn in 30. She added birdies at Nos. 14 and 17 on the way in and finished two shots behind playing partner Hye-Jin Choi, who shot 61 to take the early lead. Korda skipped the LPGA’s four-event Asia swing. She said she was burned out when the Solheim Cup matches ended in the Netherlands, and decided to take a five-day vacation in Greece. After that, she recharged at home. Korda said her favorite things during the break were cooking, sleeping in her own bed and going to the gym. "Just getting in a routine of being like a normal kind of human being," she said. "I think that's what reenergizes my batteries the most." Korda, 28, has dealt with neck problems in recent seasons and is comfortable trimming her schedule. “My body just can’t do that,” she said of the 30-event seasons some rookies play. “Once I start to feel something I just have to take that break.” She said her familiarity with Jason McDede, her caddie of eight years, gave her comfort coming back. “He knows exactly what to say, and we switch right back into that routine,” she said. Additionally, her putting coach, David Angelotti, is with her this week. Korda said their work did not change during the break and that she likes to keep things simple in her camp. “I don’t want to know all the numbers,” she said. “I just want to know a few simple keys.” Korda's return comes at a consequential time. She clinched her second Rolex Player of the Year award last week , which gave her 26 of the 27 points needed for the LPGA Hall of Fame. A win this week or at next week’s CME Group Tour Championship would earn her the last point. She would be the third-youngest player to enter the LPGA’s Hall of Fame , behind Lydia Ko and Inbee Park. Korda has won four times in 2026, including the Chevron Championship and the U.S. Women’s Open. She has good memories at the Annika, having won it three times, but commented that the Hall of Fame is not on her mind. “Is the Hall of Fame something I’m really looking at? Not at all,” she said. “I mean, I’m just focusing on being competitive and trying to give it my all. ... After that, everything else is out of my control." Well rested and inspired, Nelly Korda eyes Hall of Fame at Annika Korda hasn’t played a regular LPGA event since August but returns with some inspired footwear at this week’s Annika. item.description: Eight girls volleyball teams hailing from Lafayette Parish and the surrounding area punched their tickets to the 2026 Sugar Bowl LHSAA State Volleyball Tournament . After firing an 8-under 64 on Thursday to grab the lead after the early wave, the South African revisited his viral assessment regarding the future of former LIV Golf players following the rival circuit's financial collapse and liquidation: "Go back to Q-school." When asked if he'd received blowback from the comments, van Rooyen insisted that nobody in his circle had said much. "What kind of folks? No, no one that I hang around with. It might be people I don't know on social media. I made a comment about saying guys should go back to Q-School. I think it's completely status dependent, right? "But if a player in my position went and played Sunshine Tour for two years, I'd lose my rights to play here, so I would have to go to Q-School and find my way back, right? So isn't that fair? (AP) — Actor and race car driver Frankie Muniz has been released from a hospital following a practice-lap crash at Daytona International Speedway. The 40-year-old star of “Malcolm in the Middle” was practicing for a Proud to Honor Veterans Day Classic event, a benefit race set for Wednesday night at Daytona’s road course. “I am disappointed I won’t be able to take part in Ford’s Proud to Honor event tonight,” Muniz said in a statement. “I was looking forward to honoring the service of our veterans and racing against these other amazing drivers.” Muniz said he was a “little sore,” but the Mustang he was driving did its job to protect him. “I want to thank everyone at Ford Racing, Daytona International Speedway and the staff here at the hospital,” Muniz said. “I especially want to thank everyone who has reached out and for all the prayers.” Muniz and NASCAR driver Austin Cindric were set to represent Team Air Force in an exhibition race that benefits six nonprofits that support military and veteran communities through the Proud to Honor Fund, according to a NASCAR release. A dozen Ford Racing drivers were split into six teams to race head-to-head in Mustang Dark Horse cars in honor of a branch of the U.S. military. Musical performances by the Zac Brown Band, Russell Dickerson, Jo Dee Messina, Brittney Spencer, and Warren Zeiders were also part of the event. Muniz was nominated for an Emmy and two Golden Glove Awards for his work in “Malcolm in the Middle” and was one of the best known child actors of his time. He has also appeared in films such as “Big Fat Liar,” “Deuces Wild,” “Agent Cody Banks” and “Racing Stripes.” According to his website, Muniz took a hiatus from the entertainment world in 2006 to pursue professional racecar driving. He began competing in the Formula BMW USA Championship and later went on to race in the Champ Car Atlantic Championship from 2007-09. Muniz was fourth in the 2009 championship standings with two races to go before a season-ending injury resulted in multiple surgeries, the website said. In 2024, Muniz ran 38 races each on the NASCAR O’Reilly Auto Parts and trucks series. He’s participated in 117 trucks series races over the last three years, with one top-10 finish at Daytona in 2025.

The Yankees need Marte hitting with Rice, not instead of him Marte hit 22 homers in 2026, even as his OPS fell from .893 to .748. He’s guaranteed through 2030 with a player option for 2031. I’d walk away: Keep Rice if he’s the difference between a deal and no deal. Let Luis Garcia Jr. compete at second and spend the rest of the winter looking for another bat. 0 What do you think? item.title: Aston Villa Plan Four New Deals, One For A Man Out Until Spring: Smart Or Risky?
item.description: Aston Villa Plan Four New Deals, One For A Man Out Until Spring: Smart Or Risky? Aston Villa are preparing to tie four senior players to new contracts, according to the Telegraph, via BBC , with left-back Ian Maatsen, playmaker Emiliano Buendia and midfielders Amadou Onana and Ross Barkley all set to sign. Maatsen has already finished his. Villa confirmed on Wednesday that the Dutchman signed until 2032, two years beyond his previous deal. The club chose the November international break to settle the matter. Victor Lindelof committed to 2028 on Tuesday, teenager George Hemmings has reportedly agreed terms, and Villa have rebuilt a side that lost six starters from last season’s Europa League final. Lucas Digne’s move to Paris Saint-Germain left Maatsen as the undisputed left-back, and Manchester United’s summer interest showed Villa what waiting could cost. Results add urgency. Villa sit tenth after a 4-4 draw at Old Trafford, where they led 2-0 and 4-2 before Patrick Dorgu equalised in stoppage time. Unai Emery’s side have not won since beating Manchester City on 24 October, a run that includes a 3-0 defeat at Barcelona in the Champions League, yet they remain unbeaten in six league games. What each player offers Maatsen, 24, suits Emery’s high full-backs and has played in seven of ten league games despite a September ankle injury. After two seasons competing with Digne, he must still prove he can defend consistently in big fixtures. Buendia, 29, scored in the Europa League final and gives Emery a creative option between the lines, but his output has been uneven. He managed six league goals and two assists last season, then went seven league games without either. His contract expires next summer. Barkley, 32, has scored three Champions League goals in the first four matches and carries the ball well alongside Boubacar Kamara. His age and expiring deal make him the hardest of the four to judge. Onana, 25, brings height and defensive cover, yet he tore his ACL against the United States at the World Cup in July and looks unlikely to return before late April. Villa signed him from Everton for £50million in 2024, and his deal already runs to 2029. Are Aston Villa right to back this group with new deals? item.description: Kirk Cousins on July 11, 2023 in Los Angeles, California Credit: Randy Shropshire/Getty NEED TO KNOW Kirk Cousins said he and his wife, Julie, let their sons decide if they’d move to Minnesota after his trade to the Vikings Cousins said his wife, Julie, expressed concern about pulling the boys out of their schools and activities in Las Vegas Cousins was traded from the Las Vegas Raiders to the Vikings on Tuesday, Nov. 10 Kirk Cousins and his wife, Julie Hampton Cousins , let their sons decide the family’s next move after the quarterback was traded from the Las Vegas Raiders to the Minnesota Vikings. Cousins, 38, spoke to reporters at a Vikings press conference on Wednesday, Nov. 11, and revealed the sweet conversation Julie and their sons, Cooper and Turner , had after the trade on Tuesday, Nov. 10. “I was hoping they were going to come with me,” Cousins shared. The quarterback said he told his wife it would be “her call” to determine the family’s next move, and Julie expressed concern about pulling “the boys out of school and baseball and their friends.” Kirk and Julie Cousins on July 11, 2023 Credit: Chris Delmas/AFP/Getty After the Raiders finalized the deal with Minnesota, Julie picked up Cooper, 9, and Turner, 7, from school and shared, “Here’s the situation — dad got traded to the Minnesota Vikings,” and asked them if they’d prefer to stay in Las Vegas or relocate with their dad, he told reporters. “They looked at her, and they said, ‘Let’s go,’ ” Cousins shared. While Cousins spoke with reporters Wednesday, Julie and the kids were “across the street” in a hotel “figuring out” their next home in Minnesota, where Cousins previously spent six seasons before stints with the Falcons and Raiders. When one reporter asked if Cooper and Turner would be helping shovel snow out of their new home’s driveway, Cousins joked, “Well, we gotta get a driveway first. item.title: Boston Celtics alum Danilo Gallinari believes a 40-minute NBA game can reduce injury
item.description: MEXICO CITY - With so many injuries early in the 2026-27 NBA regular season, there has been renewed chatter among fans and analysts of the league about creative solutions to mitigate the impact of the wear and tear leading to so many players being out so early. And given his tenure with the Boston Celtics was effectively dissolved by such an injury (and marked by another serious injury earlier in his career), Danilo Gallinari has long been a supporter of cutting the playing time to 40 minutes as the game is played under FIBA rules around the globe. "If you guys have been following me and my career, I've been proposing this for at least 10 years, I think," said Gallinari to the Celtics Wire at the 2026 NBA Mexico City Game. "But of course, it would be a huge change. We were always talking to lower the number of games; I was proposing back in the day from 82 to 70. Of course it's tough to do; as players we were proposing that to the player association." "But of course the NBA and the business is like 'Okay, less games less money,' so the players were like 'Maybe not,' added the Celtics short-timer. But to go from 48 (minutes of game time) to 40 I think it would be huge for the NBA, it would be great of course." "The stats situation I think is something that will change, but the NBA is the best in the world in changing, proposing things, changing things," he added. "Players that played before never had the chance to win the (NBA) Cup. The Cup now is something new." "What about the players that didn't play the Cup? What about the players that didn't play when there was a 3-point line? They were saying, 'Oh, well, if I play with a 3-point line, what could I have done?' – all these things. So yes, why not going from 48 to 40? I think it's beneficial for everybody, for the players." Listen to "What we learned from the Boston Celtics blowout of the Philadelphia 76ers" on Spreaker.
